attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post, about the OpenAI/io device.

semantics.note: Context shows the subject is the device, not the deal. 'Real' carries some evaluative weight, but the sentence is a flat factual denial that any substantive information exists.

contract.note: The plain reading counts credible reported design constraints as information, even without a finished design. That is an ordinary reading of a flat 'no real information exists'. It is not stretched against him, though his own view was that such details were empty marketing.

evidence.note: Dated May 22, 2025, before the post. It reports WSJ coverage of an internal Altman recording: not a phone or glasses, portable, discreet, context-aware, a family of devices, shipping late 2026. These are reported plans, not specs.

reviews.rationale: Before publication, credible reporting tied to Altman's own internal remarks set out substantive intended features and limits of the device. Under the contract's fair plain reading, that is real information, so the claim that none existed is contradicted. The packet shows plans only, not finalized specifications.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. He quotes Altman's $1T line, but the category assertion and the 'nearly quadruple' arithmetic are his.

semantics.note: The proposition captures his two testable assertions and drops the personal attack on Ive. The arithmetic is treated as hypothetical, not as a forecast.

contract.note: Counting AI smart glasses in the category is a choice the evaluator made, but it is reasonable: Zitron himself brings up Glass. The contract allows a loose 'approximately fourfold' reading of 'nearly quadruple', which is fair to him.

evidence.note: Humane Ai Pin bricked in Feb 2025 after flopping. Supports failure of a prominent standalone AI gadget, not of the whole category.
The manufacturer reported 2M Ray-Ban Meta units sold and rising retention before the post. This is a company disclosure, but it is material adoption evidence against a categorical failure.
$300B post-money valuation in March 2025. Adding $1T gives 4.33x: roughly fourfold, slightly above quadruple rather than just under it.

reviews.rationale: Part of the claim holds: standalone AI companions like Humane did fail, and $1T added to $300B is about fourfold on the loose reading. The categorical claim that consumer AI devices failed to catch on is contradicted by Ray-Ban Meta's reported 2M sales and rising retention, if AI glasses are included. Strictly, 4.33x is more than 'nearly' quadruple.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition faithfully captures both parts: ChatGPT loses billions a year, and Altman has built no other new consumer product.

contract.note: Reading 'build' as launching a distinct consumer product is an ordinary reading. He may have meant a successful product, but he said no such thing. Requiring ChatGPT-specific losses, rather than OpenAI-wide losses, follows his wording.

evidence.note: Dated OpenAI launch post, Dec 2024: Sora released as a standalone consumer product at sora.com. A company disclosure, but adequate as a dated launch record. Its 2026 shutdown note is irrelevant.
A forecast of OpenAI-wide 2024 losses with some expenses excluded. It is not a ChatGPT product-level loss, so it cannot settle the financial part.

reviews.rationale: The product part is contradicted: OpenAI launched Sora as a standalone consumer product in Dec 2024, before the post. The financial part is unresolved, because the packet has only company-wide loss estimates and no ChatGPT-level accounts. Since the claim is a conjunction and one part is contradicted, the claim as a whole is contradicted.
